newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine May inflation seen unchanged - poll.
newsitem.headline: Philippine May inflation seen unchanged - poll.

text.p: Philippine annual inflation is likely to be virtually unchanged at 4.63 percent in May compared to 4.60 in April, a Reuters poll of six economists showed on Wednesday.
The projected rate is significantly lower than the 10.4 percent posted in May 1996. The actual figures are scheduled to be released on Thursday.

Economists from brokerage houses and banks agreed that steady food prices would easily offset any inflationary impact of a slight wage hike in Manila and the usual price rises in clothing and paper products before the school year starts in June.

"It's possible that it can go down further, considering we did not have any pressure on the demand side," Manuel Lim, chief economist of ING Bank Manila, said. He projected 4.5 percent inflation in May.
Manila minimum wage earners got their five peso daily wage increase in May, the second of the two-tranche mandated salary increase announced in February.
Many local firms also released workers' 13th month bonus to help cover costs of tuition and school equipment costs.
"But we have very stable food prices. Remember, it is the biggest portion in the CPI basket," Noel Reyes, research head of Anscor Hagedorn Securities said.
Food, beverages and tobacco make up 58.47 percent of the monitored basket of commodities.
He said the good harvests in the first three months of the year have meant ample food supplies, erasing any fears of another food crisis which hit the country in 1995.
The government has said it expects a slight decline in May inflation in the absence of any price shocks during the month.
While economists agreed that prices did not move up last month, some still projected the rate would firm because of a lower base last year.
"It's just a statistical abberation," Paul Joseph Garcia, economist of Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co Inc.
He predicted a 5.0 percent inflation, the highest in the poll.

The 1996 January to April inflation rates were unusually high due to the spillover of the food crisis in late 1995, leading to a corresponding unusually low rate in the same period this year, Garcia said.
"The rate is normalising, so there might be a higher year-on-year change ... In terms of month-on-month change, we might see zero growth," he added.
Economists said inflation is no longer a major concern despite a strong economic recovery.
The government recently cut its 1997 inflation target to between 5.2 to 5.7 percent, closer to regional levels.

"The inflation problem has already been put on the backburner for a while...We have low inflation, low interests rate and a steady foreign exchange. This will definitely lead to a sustainable growth," ING's Lim said.
The following is the different forecast given by the six brokerages:
Anscor Hagedorn Securities 4.3 to 4.5
All AsiaCapital Trust 4.8 to 4.9
Capitol Securities One 4.5 to 4.8
DBS Securities 4.3 to 4.5
ING Bank 4.5
Metrobank 5.0
Average 4.63
-- Manila Newsroom (63 2) 841 8934
